responsibility: This module contains GCC’s documentation sources and documentation-build support, defining the stable manuals that describe GCC for both users and compiler developers. Its top-level Texinfo manuals such as gcc.texi, gccint.texi, install.texi, cpp.texi, and gm2.texi assemble the user guide, internals manual, installation guide, preprocessor manual, and language-specific manuals, while numerous chapter and fragment files document major compiler subsystems and concepts including invocation and options, language standards and extensions, bug reporting and troubleshooting, coverage and profiling tools, collect2 and libgcc, front-end architecture, passes, GENERIC, GIMPLE, Tree SSA, CFG and loop infrastructure, RTL, LTO, plugins, machine descriptions, target hooks, portability, build/configuration machinery, and UX guidance for diagnostics. The module also includes generated target-option reference material such as AVR and RISC-V option tables, shared include files for licensing and common Texinfo macros, and Sphinx configuration for standalone documentation subtrees, making gcc/doc the source of GCC’s user-facing and developer-facing reference documentation rather than a compiler execution stage itself.
